name: cv-baseline
hypothesis: Reference point for the post-2026-09-08 era: frozen YAMNet linear probe, Dropout(0.2), Adam 0.002, label_smoothing 0.2, translation general, medium at 5 rotating folds, plus the two correctness fixes the archived log supports — per-class weighting inside the loss (weighted_bce_loss) instead of fit(class_weight=), and restoring the true val_loss argmin (RestoreTrueBest) instead of the last min_delta-clearing epoch.
conclusion: THE BASELINE every experiment in this era compares against. 0.218 mean sens@fpr0.005 over 5 rotating folds. Baseline field here is a pre-fix control (identical data/folds/config, neither fix applied), not a target: the two fixes measured -0.006, 1 fold up / 2 down / 2 flat, i.e. INSIDE the noise floor and in the opposite direction to the archive, which had them at +0.013 (class-weight-fix, 7/11) and +0.008 (restore-on-sens, 9 up/0 down) on the pre-revision 11-fold set. They are kept anyway because both are correctness fixes independent of the metric: Keras' fit(class_weight=) collapses a multi-hot target to argmax(y) and scales the whole sample by one scalar, so a buzz frame co-occurring with an earlier-indexed class never got ins_buzz's weight at all; and stock EarlyStopping snapshots the last epoch beating min_delta, discarding every smaller later improvement. Note the fixes did change training materially (best_epoch 87->174 on Fit+Fast, 79->147 on 1_95; mean activation -1.59 -> -2.70 on JamesU) — the metric simply did not move outside noise. Caveat on all of it: 5 folds gives weak discrimination, and 2 of the 5 (both Diel Drivers) sit near chance at 0.021/0.037 and were byte-identical across both runs, so only 3 folds actually moved.

name: context-embedder
hypothesis: Revalidate the archived context-embedder win on the post-2026-09-08 data: yamnet_context embeds concat(t-1, t, t+1) of real neighbouring audio inside the embedder (3072-d), so the frame grid and labels are unchanged but each frame's feature window is 2.88s. Ported from refs/archive/context-embedder onto the current three-layer extractor.
conclusion: REVALIDATED AND LARGER: 0.218 -> 0.258 (+0.040) vs +0.022 on the old 11-fold data. 3 folds up / 2 down, but the split is not even: the 3 up are the only folds with enough buzz to measure (305-2144 buzz frames, +0.037/+0.069/+0.125, all well outside the ~0.014 noise floor) and the 2 down are the near-chance Diel Drivers pair, where -0.007 is ~1 buzz frame of 146 and -0.023 is ~10 of 433. Ships as-is (probe sizes input from n_embeddings; inference calls the same embed()). Extraction ~11min/982MB, CV ~19min (~2x baseline, 3x input dims). Willard GAINED (+0.037), so willard-regression did not reproduce; frame sensitivity by event span shows short buzz gaining MORE than long (+0.046 vs +0.026), so the dilution story is unsupported. Next: yamnet-combined is the other unrevalidated clean win, run it alone before asking whether the two compose. See notes.md for diagnostics: 7 file-spanning annotations supply 63%/52% of the two top folds' buzz frames; the two near-chance folds fail oppositely (1_150 = buzz indistinguishable from its own background, 1_95 = mech_auto false positives set its threshold); and trill is NOT the dominant confuser (mech_auto 75 > ambient_background 46 > ins_trill 43).

name: harmonic-comb
hypothesis: Give the frozen probe an explicit f0 channel: yamnet_harmonic = YAMNet 1024-d (byte-identical) + a 77-d handcrafted block (40-d harmonic comb profile over f0 candidates 70-450 Hz with 6 harmonics and off-comb subtraction; comb peak/soft-argmax f0; 24-d band contrast; 8-d within-frame amplitude modulation; flatness+ZCR). All log10 ratios against a same-frame reference on RMS-normalised frames, so gain-invariant (3.4e-4 across 20 dB) with no fitted statistics and hence no cross-fold leakage. Aimed at 1_95, whose fpr0.005 threshold is set by 32 mech_auto frames of 35: engine (~90 Hz) and wingbeat (~220 Hz) combs differ in f0, which supp-freq's four global scalars could not resolve.
conclusion: INCONCLUSIVE, and the run that says so is a repeat of itself. Run 1 gave 0.223 (+0.005, 3 up/2 down). A second CV of the IDENTICAL config gave 0.239 (+0.021, 4 up/1 down) — the two runs differ by +0.016 headline, 3 up/1 down/1 flat, from TF nondeterminism alone (no seed control). The effect is bounded above by the repeat spread, so nothing separates the comb block from noise. 1_150 alone moved 0.007 -> 0.062 between identical runs on 146 buzz frames. Independently confirms noise-floor-cv (~0.014) at 0.016 on the CURRENT 5-fold roster, with the noise concentrated in thin folds (>1000-buzz-frame folds moved 0.019/0.013, 1_150 moved 0.055). MECHANISM FAILED AT ITS TARGET: 1_95 moved +0.002 in both runs and was the only byte-stable fold across two nondeterministic runs — structural, not stochastic. But the block is NOT inert: fold weights (now saved) show the comb dims carry 1.29x the per-dim |w| of a YAMNet dim on ins_buzz in all 5 folds, and the 40-d comb profile specifically 1.64x. Used, weighted preferentially, changes nothing => the f0 information is REDUNDANT with YAMNet's representation, a better-evidenced version of supp-freq-v2's claim. This closes handcrafted frequency features on the strongest form of the idea, current data, current metric; a learnable filterbank is untried but the redundancy argues against it. Carry-over worth keeping: 03_train now saves fold model weights (~212 KB/fold, optimizer shipped-only).

name: combined-revalidate
hypothesis: Revalidate the archived yamnet-combined win on the post-2026-09-08 data: concat YAMNet's 1024-d embedding with the 521 AudioSet sigmoid scores from the head above it (1545-d), so the probe gets AudioSet's Insect/Bee/Buzz/Engine decision boundaries as ready-made features instead of relearning them. Old delta +0.016 at 7/11 folds. Run alone against cv_baseline before asking whether it composes with context-embedder. Rebuilt the missing yamnet_combined.keras (embedding block verified byte-identical to shipped yamnet).
conclusion: INCONCLUSIVE, do not build on it. +0.010, 2 folds up / 3 down, against the 0.016 repeat-run spread harmonic-comb measured on this same 5-fold roster — smaller than the noise and split in direction, which is LOOP.md's definition of a result not to act on. Not a negative either: the direction matches the archive's +0.016 and 5 folds cannot resolve an effect that size. Movers do not tell a story (willard +0.050 at 305 buzz frames is the thinnest non-degenerate fold; mustard +0.028 at 2144 is barely above its own measured 0.019 repeat movement; the 3 down folds are all within 0.010). NOT composed with context-embedder — IDEAS.md's precondition was that it stand on its own. One clean structural finding: it reaches the SAME val_loss in fewer epochs on every long-training fold (mustard 162->129, Fit+Fast 174->130, best_val_loss identical to 4dp) — the sigmoid scores are a supervised readout of the block beside them, so same destination by a shorter path, not new information. DIAGNOSTIC FOR THE STANDARDIZATION FOLLOW-UP, measured live: the two blocks are 8x apart in mean per-dim sd (0.089 vs 0.011) and 13x in magnitude, confirming the archived ~10x caution; and ~120 of the 521 sigmoid dims have sd<1e-4 (AudioSet classes that never fire on this corpus), which is exactly the population that makes a Keras Normalization layer divide by sqrt(1e-7) and blow up to NaN. Mask or drop those before adapting. Embeddings (506MB) and the rebuilt keras file are in the shared tree, so the follow-up needs no re-extraction.

name: standardize-blocks
hypothesis: yamnet_combined's 1545-d input mixes a 1024-d YAMNet block with 521 sigmoid scores at ~8x the per-dim sd; under one Adam LR the small block is underweighted, so per-dim standardization (fold-safe, fit on the training pool only) should let it contribute.
conclusion: Negative despite a +0.031 headline: the entire gain is fold 1_150 (+0.151), the 146-buzz-frame fold that moved 0.007->0.062 between two identical runs. Both rich folds are flat (1_29 0.000, Fit+Fast -0.003), and the mean delta over the other four folds is +0.001. All folds converged (502-1000 epochs vs a 3000 cap), so this is not a truncation artifact -- standardization simply costs ~6x the epochs for no measured gain. --standardize kept in the code, off by default; not adopted.

name: perch-probe
hypothesis: Perch v2's bioacoustic training domain, not YAMNet's AudioSet domain, is what limits the frozen probe; a Perch embedding should beat YAMNet above the noise floor.
conclusion: Inconclusive, leaning negative. Headline 0.244 vs 0.218 (+0.026), but the entire gain is in the two thinnest folds and tracks frame-length dilution, not the embedder: overlap_event_s scales with framelength, so Perch's 5.0s frame demands 1.0s of overlap to label a frame vs YAMNet's 0.192s, 31% of buzz events are shorter than that, and Perch ends up labelling 17970 frame-seconds as buzz against YAMNet's 9618. Per-fold dilution predicts the delta exactly: the two folds at ~2.9x dilution gained +0.131 each, the fold at 1.22x (1_29, the richest, 2144 buzz frames) lost 0.195. Thresholds also rest on ~5-7 negative frames vs the baseline's ~24-35. The only unconfounded evidence points against the hypothesis. Next step is YAMNet at a matched 5s frame, not another Perch run.

name: aves-probe
hypothesis: AVES (aves-base-bio, wav2vec2 pretrained on bioacoustics), final transformer layer, 768-d, as a drop-in for YAMNet's frozen 1024-d embedding under cv-baseline's exact probe config; prerequisite for IDEA E1's middle-layer sweep.
conclusion: Clear negative, and clean: 0.218 -> 0.074 (-0.144), 5 folds down and 0 up, with the two rich folds carrying it (1_29 -0.410, Fit+Fast -0.220) — 26x the ~0.016 noise floor. AVES's 1.0s frame vs YAMNet's 0.96s moved overlap_event_s only 0.192 -> 0.200, and the dilution check that sank perch-probe passes here: buzz rate per fold is unchanged to three decimals (1_29 0.2815 -> 0.2801), so the headline joins cv_baseline directly. Recomputing the parked 2026-06 geometry diagnostic on current medium INVERTS it: AVES mean |Cohen d| 0.242 vs YAMNet 0.155, mean |AUC-0.5| 0.074 vs 0.022 — the 0.13-vs-0.23 claim was a scale artifact of YAMNet being 89.6% exact zeros. YAMNet wins only where signal is concentrated (top-10 dims 0.260 vs 0.226, max |d| 1.91 vs 0.91). Closing E1 on CV magnitude, not on geometry: a middle layer would have to find ~0.15 sensitivity the final layer has nowhere. The live lead is a non-linear head over AVES's distributed representation, parked under the 1-layer injunction. Extraction is now 1.0h not 14.3h (main 8fe1336) and medium's AVES embeddings are cached.
amended: 2026-09-09: trust clean -> caveated. The measurement stands; the conclusion overreached. Superseded on mechanism by aves-readout: the probe was UNDERTRAINED, not beaten. val_sens rises monotonically to the final epoch in all 5 folds (best at or within 2 epochs of the last), EarlyStopping halts on a val_loss plateau, and training is ~2 gradient steps/epoch (size_batch 65568 vs ~72k frames). A converged offline linear readout of the SAME cached embeddings reaches 0.194 vs the 0.074 logged here. AVES is still worse than YAMNet under a matched readout (0.194 vs 0.261; 0.229 vs 0.468 on 1_29), so the direction holds and the magnitude was inflated ~2.5x by the head. Do not cite this entry as an embedder verdict without reading aves-readout.

name: aves-readout
hypothesis: aves-probe's -0.144 is a readout failure, not an embedder failure: the buzz information is in the AVES embeddings (better per-dimension separation than YAMNet) but the shipped probe cannot extract it. Test by sweeping readouts offline on the cached embeddings, YAMNet as control.
method_note: NOT A PIPELINE NUMBER. sklearn LogisticRegression (lbfgs, max_iter 2000, class_weight balanced, binary ins_buzz) over cached embeddings, scored through 03_train/metrics.py:sens_at_fpr on the same 5-fold rotation. Differs from the Keras probe in loss, class weighting, label smoothing, optimiser and multi-label structure simultaneously. Ranks readouts; does not join cv_baseline.
conclusion: Confirmed on outcome, wrong on mechanism, and the useful finding is about the pipeline rather than AVES. Offline the same AVES embeddings reach 0.194 vs the 0.074 aves-probe logged, so ~2.5x of that verdict was the head. But the cause is not overfitting as hypothesised: the training pool is 43 folds (not 5), val_sens rises monotonically to the final epoch in all 5 folds, and the probe trains at ~2 gradient steps/epoch (size_batch 65568 vs ~72k frames) before EarlyStopping halts it on a val_loss plateau. The probe is UNDERTRAINED. Consistent with regularisation strength barely mattering (YAMNet spans 0.253-0.261 over C=1e-3..10; AVES 0.143-0.193, already +0.069 over the Keras probe at its most constrained setting). The control is the headline: YAMNet also lifts, 0.218 -> 0.261, so the shipped probe leaves ~0.043 on the table for cv_baseline itself. archive restore-on-sens is the indicated lever and its shelving rationale ('the frozen probe's val_loss barely diverges from sens') is a YAMNet statement that is false for AVES. PCA is the one clean geometry result and it inverts the hypothesis's own prediction: YAMNet keeps 90% of its sensitivity in 16 principal directions, AVES 28%, needing ~256 to reach 94% - concentrated vs distributed, measured. AVES remains genuinely worse under matched converged readouts (0.194 vs 0.261; 0.229 vs 0.468 on 1_29). Next: grid IDEAS L1-L9 on YAMNet, L1 (restore-on-sens) first.

name: probe-grid
hypothesis: IDEAS L1-L7 probe-convergence grid on YAMNet: the probe does ~2 gradient steps/epoch and stops on a val_loss plateau while val_sens still rises, so stopping/steps levers should recover the 0.218->0.261 offline-readout gap.
conclusion: L1 (--monitor val_sens) is the only lever that pays: 0.241/0.257 over two draws vs baseline 0.218/0.227/0.208 (n=3, mean 0.2177, SD 0.0095), +0.031, no overlap between the configs' draws. The gain is a hard-deployment gain concentrated in 1_150 (0.021 tight over 3 baseline draws -> 0.089/0.158); willard is not evidence (baseline alone spans 0.180-0.233). The motivating hypothesis is DISPROVED: L3 batch-size 4096 (9x steps/epoch) +0.003, L2 min_delta 0 -0.001, L4 epoch cap never binds — the probe converges fine, it was scored on the wrong curve. L6 label_smoothing 0.05 did not replicate (0.233 then 0.197, mean -0.003) and L1+L6 do not stack (+0.005). L5 dropout both directions and L7 weight decay dead. Minimum detectable effect at n=1 is ~0.027, which rules out everything except L1. Flags added (all defaulting to the old hardcoded values); adopting --monitor val_sens is the follow-up. See notes.md.
amended: 2026-09-09 (monitor-leakage): L1 (--monitor val_sens) is the entry's headline lever, and it does not survive removing the held-out-fold selection leakage. The held-out fold is its own monitor, so a val_sens run reports max-over-epochs of the reported statistic. Re-scored at a cross-fold epoch, the +0.031 becomes +0.007 (0.216 -> 0.223), inside this entry's own 0.0095 SD. The rest of the grid stands, and its null verdicts are unaffected or improve. | 2026-09-09 (xfold-epoch): magnitude superseded, direction stands. monitor-leakage re-scored this entry with curves TRUNCATED at each fold's patience tail, which caps the cross-fold epoch on 4 of 5 folds and systematically penalises any config that ships near its peak. On a fixed 400-epoch budget with no truncation the leak measures +0.021, not the ~0.04-0.05 implied here, and the honest value of context+late-stopping is 0.288 (not 0.263/0.264). Keep trust=artifact: the reported number is still inflated and still not comparable at face value. See exp/xfold-epoch:notes/new-era.md before reusing any number from this entry.

name: mech-margin
hypothesis: mech_auto is the plurality of cv_baseline's threshold-setting false positives (58/219 pooled; 32 of 35 at Diel Drivers/2026-05-06/1_95, the only fold with a positive threshold), so a class-conditional hinge lam*1[mech_auto and not ins_buzz]*relu(z_buzz+m) pushing the buzz logit below -m on vehicle frames should lift sens@fpr0.005, concentrated at 1_95. Deterministic per-frame, no within-batch rank, so unlike the archived tail-loss OHEM term val_loss stays a valid early-stopping monitor. Run as a 4-point geometric dose ladder (lam 0.125/0.5/2.0/8.0 at m=2.0) since a single-run comparison has an MDE of ~0.027.
conclusion: CLEAR NEGATIVE, monotone across a 64x dose ladder: lam 0.125/0.5/2.0/8.0 -> 0.202/0.169/0.090/0.021 (-0.016/-0.049/-0.128/-0.197), 5 folds down 0 up at every dose at or above 0.5, with the two rich folds (2144 and 1031 buzz frames) carrying the largest losses. Well outside probe-grid's ~0.027 MDE. 1_95, the fold it was built for, is DOWN at every dose. MECHANISM, and it is the useful part: the mech_auto SHARE of threshold-setting FPs RISES with the dose (58/219=26.5% baseline -> 63/196=32.1% at lam 0.5 -> 68/173=39.3% at lam 2.0), i.e. the term lost rank on the very class it was penalising while pushing it down in absolute terms. What it actually did is collapse the buzz/non-buzz mean-logit gap (1_29 1.578 -> 1.000 -> 0.519; 1_95 0.513 -> 0.272 -> -0.064, inverted): both populations fall, buzz falls faster. NOT weight collinearity - cosine(W_ins_buzz, W_mech_auto) = -0.016 in cv_baseline's readout, near-orthogonal and 10th of 14 (ins_trill +0.268, ambient_background +0.265 are the aligned ones); the overlap is in the FRAME population, which is why mech_auto tops the FP census at all. GENERAL LESSON: the margin is specified in absolute logit space while the metric reads only RANK (every fold is thresholded on its own held-out audio), so driving a subpopulation below a fixed logit buys nothing - it can only help by rotating the readout, and rotating away from mech_auto frames rotates away from buzz. Any future confuser penalty should be PAIRWISE (buzz frame above confuser frame), not absolute. Closes the 'buzz-vs-mech_auto margin' lead that IDEAS.md named twice as the remaining candidate for 1_95.

name: shared-trunk-head
hypothesis: The probe head is Dropout->Dense(15): 15 decoupled logistic regressions, so no gradient runs from a mech_auto error to W[:, ins_buzz]. A shared ReLU hidden layer (Dropout->Dense(h,relu)->Dropout->Dense(15)) gives all 15 classes one learned representation, so auxiliary-class supervision can shape features the buzz neuron uses. This is the multi-task-transfer claim, distinct from the capacity claim MLP heads were closed on in E1/E2. Step (1) of the IDEAS sequencing: hidden layer alone, uniform loss. Run as a width ladder h=64/256/1024 because probe-grid put the single-run MDE at ~0.027.
conclusion: NULL across a 16x width ladder: h=64/256/1024 -> 0.219/0.221/0.226 (+0.001/+0.003/+0.008), folds split 3up/2down at every width. Every delta is inside probe-grid's ~0.027 MDE, and the top headline sits inside the baseline's own n=3 range (0.208/0.218/0.227, SD 0.0095). Not a negative (no width hurt) but no gain to bank. MECHANISM TESTED AND ANSWERED: mech-margin failed because a LINEAR readout cannot push mech_auto frames down without taking buzz with it, and the live hypothesis was that a non-linear stage could; given one, 1_95 -- the fold it was aimed at -- does not move at any width (-0.005/+0.002/-0.007), nor does 1_150. The non-noise-shaped residue is a stable TRADE between the two rich folds: 1_29 gains ~+0.03 and Fit+Fast loses at all three widths, both above the ~0.019 repeat movement for >1000-buzz folds, neither flipping sign across three runs; the mean is null because they cancel, and widening only shrinks the Fit+Fast loss (-0.043->-0.007). Convergence diagnostic: the trunk reaches the SAME mean best_val_loss (0.9064-0.9075 vs baseline 0.9101) in 2.5x fewer epochs (46.6 vs 114.8 at h=1024) -- same destination, shorter path, the signature combined-revalidate found for the AudioSet sigmoid block. Reading: YAMNet's 1024-d code already carries what a shared trunk would learn; the head was not the constraint. IDEAS step (2) (per-neuron buzz weighting on top) is unblocked but no longer motivated -- its premise was that weighting needs something to be weighted against, and the trunk provides that for no gain. --hidden kept in code, default 0.

name: context-monitor
hypothesis: The era's only two clean gains — yamnet_context (+0.040, carried by the 3 folds with enough buzz to resolve) and probe-grid's L1 --monitor val_sens (+0.031, carried entirely by 1_150) — pay on disjoint folds and share no mechanism, so they should compose additively to ~0.29. Falsifier: landing at ~0.258 (the larger component alone) would mean they compete for the same headroom. Comparator is context_embedder, so the single variable is the monitor.
conclusion: COMPOSES, ADDITIVELY, AND IT IS THE ERA'S BEST: 0.307. Against context_embedder +0.049 (4 up/1 down); against cv_baseline +0.089 with 5 folds up / 0 down, the only all-up run in the log. Sum of the parts is +0.071 vs +0.089 observed, the +0.018 excess inside noise, so additive rather than synergistic; the falsifier did not fire. Each component keeps its own fold: context carries the rich ones (1_29 0.426->0.551 alone, monitor alone flat there at 0.431/0.421) and the monitor carries 1_150 (0.089/0.158 alone, while context ALONE makes it worse, 0.021->0.014). MECHANISM, not variance: context_embedder shipped best_epoch 5 on 1_150 — under val_loss the 3072-d model hits its argmin almost immediately and the fold was scored on a barely-trained probe (0.014, precision 0.077); with val_sens it ships epoch 160 for 0.219. A wider input has an earlier val_loss argmin, so the monitor is load-bearing FOR the context embedder rather than an independent hyperparameter win. Same signature runs the other way at Fit+Fast (144->17, -0.029). CAVEAT ON THE SIZE (why caveated): over the other four folds the mean delta vs context_embedder is +0.0095, i.e. nothing — the +0.049 is 1_150, the 146-buzz-frame fold that moved 0.007->0.062 between two identical baseline runs. This reproduces probe-grid's L1 finding rather than adding to it. Arguing for the direction anyway: 1_150's 0.219 is above the top of its range over ~8 draws this era (previous max 0.158), and the epoch-5 diagnostic gives it a cause. 1_95 still near chance (0.044) — the 4th intervention not to move it. Next: (1) --monitor val_sens as the default is now more than a tidy-up, it is load-bearing for the best config; (2) one 17-min repeat of THIS config to see whether 1_150 holds near 0.219 before anyone builds on 0.307.
amended: 2026-09-09 (monitor-leakage): the +0.049 over context_embedder is selection optimism, not composition. Under a cross-fold epoch rule applied identically to both, context_embedder scores 0.277 and this config 0.264 — paired 2 up / 3 down, and 1_150 (which carries the whole claim) flips 0.144 -> 0.075. The 1_150 stopping failure this entry correctly identified is real but is fixed by the epoch rule alone, without the monitor. The context embedder itself is unaffected and gets larger (+0.040 -> +0.061); only the monitor half is withdrawn. | 2026-09-09 (xfold-epoch): magnitude superseded, direction stands. monitor-leakage re-scored this entry with curves TRUNCATED at each fold's patience tail, which caps the cross-fold epoch on 4 of 5 folds and systematically penalises any config that ships near its peak. On a fixed 400-epoch budget with no truncation the leak measures +0.021, not the ~0.04-0.05 implied here, and the honest value of context+late-stopping is 0.288 (not 0.263/0.264). Keep trust=artifact: the reported number is still inflated and still not comparable at face value. See exp/xfold-epoch:notes/new-era.md before reusing any number from this entry.

name: context-monitor-r2
hypothesis: Confirmation repeat of context-monitor (yamnet_context + --monitor val_sens, 0.307), the era's best config: an independent draw of the identical config, since there is no seed control. Tests (1) whether the headline holds near 0.307 and (2) the one genuinely n=1 part, 1_150's 0.219, which topped the era's four val_sens runs by 0.048. Falsifier: headline at or below 0.258 (context alone) with 1_150 back under 0.10.
conclusion: CONFIRMED, AND 1_150 REPRODUCED EXACTLY. 0.307 -> 0.312 (+0.005) against a 0.0095 single-run SD: two draws indistinguishable, mean 0.310, and this draw is again 5 folds up / 0 down vs cv_baseline (+0.094). The falsifier did not fire. 1_150 landed on 0.219 a second time from a different training run (best_epoch 160 -> 192); the fold's granularity is 1/146, so both runs detected exactly 32 of 146 buzz frames. The era's val_sens group on that fold is now 0.089/0.158/0.171/0.219/0.219 against a val_loss group of 0.007-0.062 -- still disjoint, and the composed config sits above the monitor-alone maximum (0.158) twice, so the context x monitor lift on 1_150 is real rather than a draw. NEW OBSERVATION: under val_sens the stopping epoch is bimodal on RICH folds -- Fit+Fast/53 shipped epoch 17 (0.465) and epoch 226 (0.520) across the two identical runs, a 0.055 swing, the same early-vs-late ambiguity context-monitor saw run the other way there. Most of this config's run-to-run spread now comes from the rich folds, a reversal of the usual pattern. Cheap follow-up, no training needed: val_sens_fpr0.005_curve is persisted per fold, so a tie-break rule (prefer the later of two comparable peaks, or smooth before argmax) can be replayed offline. 1_95 still near chance at 0.039 -- the fifth intervention not to move it.
amended: 2026-09-09 (monitor-leakage): the confirmation confirms the leakage, not the effect. Honest headline 0.262 against r1's 0.264 — the two draws do reproduce, at a value below context_embedder's 0.277. 1_150 hitting 0.219 in both draws at epochs 160 and 192 is 32/146 twice: the ceiling of a 1/146-granular statistic maximised over ~200 epochs, which is what this entry read as exact reproducibility. | 2026-09-09 (xfold-epoch): magnitude superseded, direction stands. monitor-leakage re-scored this entry with curves TRUNCATED at each fold's patience tail, which caps the cross-fold epoch on 4 of 5 folds and systematically penalises any config that ships near its peak. On a fixed 400-epoch budget with no truncation the leak measures +0.021, not the ~0.04-0.05 implied here, and the honest value of context+late-stopping is 0.288 (not 0.263/0.264). Keep trust=artifact: the reported number is still inflated and still not comparable at face value. See exp/xfold-epoch:notes/new-era.md before reusing any number from this entry.

name: monitor-leakage
hypothesis: Each rotation's held-out fold IS its early-stopping monitor (train.py:568), so --monitor val_sens reports max-over-epochs of the exact statistic it is scored on. README:642 argues that optimism is small, but every clause of that argument is specific to val_loss. Test it with no training: re-score every run's folds at an epoch chosen from the OTHER folds' persisted val_sens curves (README:651's own prescription).
conclusion: --monitor val_sens DOES NOT SURVIVE removing the leakage; the context embedder does, and gets larger. Offline re-scoring of all 26 runs of the era (tools/honest_epoch.py, no training). Mechanical confirmation first: peak-at_best of val_sens_fpr0.005_curve is exactly 0.000 on all 5 folds of every val_sens run, non-zero on every val_loss run. Under an identical cross-fold epoch rule the val_loss arm is unmoved (0.218->0.216, n=3) and the val_sens arm drops (0.249->0.223, n=2; context 0.310->0.263, n=2). Monitor effect: +0.031 -> +0.007 on yamnet (inside the 0.0095 SD), +0.052 -> -0.014 on context. Context embedder: +0.040 -> +0.061. Best honest config is yamnet_context ALONE at 0.277, above context_monitor's 0.263, paired 2 up/3 down. 1_150 is the whole story and is a selection artifact: context_embedder's own curve already reaches 0.144 (its 0.014 epoch-5 stop is a real but separately-fixable failure), while context_monitor's 0.219 sits at epoch 160/192 where the other four folds put the shared optimum at 19/27, uncapped. The famous non-overlapping monitor split on 1_150 closes completely under the honest rule (val_sens 0.055-0.123 inside val_loss 0.000-0.165; medians 0.075 vs 0.068; the six highest are val_loss runs). 0.219 twice at different epochs is 32/146 twice, i.e. maximising a 1/146-granular statistic, not reproducibility. Also drops perch_probe 0.244->0.169 and RAISES shared-trunk-head's hidden_1024 0.226->0.253. No confirming CV is owed: re-scoring at epoch e from the persisted curve IS the model's score at epoch e. The follow-up that does cost a CV is making cross-fold epoch selection the shipped rule, which needs a fixed epoch budget because early stopping truncates the curves.
amended: 2026-09-09 (xfold-epoch): the mechanical finding stands exactly -- peak==at_best on every val_sens fold -- and so does the direction. The MAGNITUDES are truncation-limited and overstate the leak: this entry's own tool caps the cross-fold epoch at the shortest other-fold curve, which penalises peak-shipping configs specifically. Measured untruncated, the leak is +0.021 and late stopping is worth a REAL +0.031, so context-monitor's +0.049 was ~60% real rather than wholly artifact. 'Best honest config is yamnet_context alone at 0.277' is superseded: 0.277 was this tool's lower bound; the untruncated best is yamnet_context + cross-fold epochs at 0.288. trust stays clean -- the measurement was correct for what it could see. | 2026-09-11 (audit): the val_loss arm's '+0.000, 6 down/8 up' is confirmed and strengthened -- re-measured untruncated across 17 runs it is -0.002, 8 up/9 down. So the entry's own control group is the evidence that val_loss stopping carries no measurable optimism, and only the val_sens arm is leakage. The val_sens magnitude is budget-dependent (own-peak minus xfold-pooled: +0.021 at a 400-epoch budget, mean +0.006 over the five 150-epoch runs on disk), so quote it with its budget.

name: xfold-epoch
hypothesis: Cross-fold epoch selection as the shipped rule (IDEAS' highest-value open item). Each rotation's held-out fold is also its early-stopping monitor, so every logged number was scored at an epoch chosen from the fold it scores. honest_epoch.py estimated the fix at +0.019 on context_embedder, but that estimate is truncation-limited: early stopping cuts each curve at its own patience tail, so the pooled epoch is capped by the shortest other-fold curve and lands on the cap for 4 of 5 folds in every run on disk. Train a fixed 400-epoch budget with no early stopping so nothing is truncated, snapshot weights per epoch, then score each fold at the argmax of the OTHER four folds' mean sens curve. Control is NOT a second CV: the same trajectories are also scored where RestoreTrueBest would have restored, so the two rules are compared on one draw, well under the ~0.027 single-run MDE.
conclusion: ADOPT, AND IT SEPARATES TWO CLAIMS THE LOOP HAS BEEN CONFLATING. Three rules off one run, untruncated: own-peak (what a --monitor val_sens run reports) 0.309, xfold 0.288, earlystop 0.257. Validity check: the replayed earlystop control reproduces the original context_embedder run's 0.258 to 0.001 from an independent draw. Decomposition: val_sens selection optimism = +0.021; genuine late-stopping gain = +0.031. context-monitor's +0.049 = 0.031 real + 0.021 leak (sum 0.052), so that result was ~60% real, ~40% artifact. Paired vs context_embedder: +0.030, 2 up / 3 down. THE SHAPE MATTERS MORE THAN THE HEADLINE: this is insurance, not improvement. On the four folds whose early stopping picked a sane epoch (61-155) xfold averages -0.008 -- a pooled epoch is a compromise. On the one that broke, 1_150/apple at epoch 6 (a 3072-d input hits its val_loss argmin immediately, scoring a barely-trained probe at 0.027), xfold picks 141 and gets 0.199, +0.185. -0.008 is half a per-fold SD; +0.185 is ~11x it. The point is not the sensitivity, it is that a stopping failure can no longer masquerade as a result -- the exact mechanism by which aves-probe logged 0.074 as an embedder verdict. BUDGET: the POOLED curve is flat from e145-400 (253/397 epochs within 0.005 of max) while per-fold argmaxes scatter over 19-337, so the rule only needs to land in a plateau; e250 costs 0.001, e150 0.004, e100 0.016. Use 250. SUPERSEDES: IDEAS' 'best-known config, honest 0.277' -- that was honest_epoch.py's truncated lower bound; untruncated it is 0.288. THIS ENDS THE ERA rather than re-baselining it, since the rule moves every number by a config-dependent amount. Luke approved the finding but is not ready for the refactor as of 2026-09-09; the full cutover procedure, expected numbers, falsifiers and entries needing re-run are in exp/xfold-epoch:notes/new-era.md, with the methodology and literature in exp/xfold-epoch:notes/epoch-selection.md.
amended: 2026-09-11 (audit, exp/pairwise-rank:notes/new-era-audit.md): measurement stands, ATTRIBUTION AND PRESCRIPTION SUPERSEDED. (1) The gain is not removal of selection leakage. Across all 17 val_loss-stopped runs on disk, shipped minus xfold-pooled averages -0.002 (8 up/9 down, range -0.038..+0.075) -- no measurable optimism in the val_loss arm; README's 'bounded, and small' for val_loss is confirmed, not refuted. What early stopping does is UNDERTRAIN: 1_150 stops at epoch 5-32 under every embedder tried. (2) Recomputed paired from folds_sx.csv, the four healthy folds cost -0.004 (not -0.008) and 1_150 gains +0.172 (not +0.185), so 110% of the +0.031 headline is one fold. (3) --epoch-rule xfold is superseded by --fixed-epochs (2026-09-10), which selects no epoch at all and is within 0.006 of xfold on every fixed-budget run on disk, ahead on 4 of 6 -- including this run's own config, where a plain fixed e250 scores 0.294 against xfold's 0.288. (4) 'Budget 250' was measured here only; yavf_h0/h256/h1024 and yavx_h1024 are all still rising at their 150-epoch cap, so 250 is a floor. (5) The '+0.021 leak' is budget-dependent: +0.021 at 400 epochs, mean +0.006 over the five 150-epoch runs. trust stays clean -- everything reported was correctly measured on the run it was measured on.

name: buzz-selector-curves
hypothesis: Instrumentation for IDEAS 'buzz-only low-variance selection statistic': log val_auc_buzz and val_ce_buzz per epoch alongside val_sens_fpr0.005, persist all as curves in summary.json, then compare the three (plus incumbent val_loss) as epoch selectors offline. No training change; stopping rule untouched. Falsifier: if the pooled sens plateau is wide, any selector landing in it scores the same and a stabler statistic buys nothing.
conclusion: Curves adopted (cheap, survive data revisions). Buzz-only-selector lead CLOSED NEGATIVE: under a non-leaking cross-fold epoch rule all four statistics (val_loss, sens@fpr0.005, auc_buzz, ce_buzz) return IDENTICAL per-fold sensitivities [0.20,0.41,0.38,0.04,0.09] and mean (~0.222 truncated / ~0.235 untruncated), because the pooled sens curve is flat e129-164 so any in-plateau selector scores the same. Falsifier fired. Premise (AUC lower variance) had already failed IDEAS' bootstrap. Independently reproduces xfold-epoch: early stopping healthy on 3 folds, broke on 1_11 (e54) and 1_150 (e21); cross-fold rule lifts 1_150 0.048->0.09, flat-to-negative on healthy folds. Headline 0.226 is a clean 4th baseline draw (0.208/0.218/0.227/0.226, mean 0.220 — no drift). n=1 but the cross-statistic identity of results is structural (shared plateau), not stochastic. Epoch selection remains xfold-epoch's question (deferred), not a monitor choice.
amended: 2026-09-11 (audit): this entry CLOSES the 'buzz-only selector' lead that exp/xfold-epoch:notes/new-era.md still lists as open -- it was committed 71 seconds after that file and the file never saw it. new-era.md and notes/epoch-selection.md have been marked accordingly. The structural finding (a wide pooled plateau makes every in-plateau selector score identically) is also the reason the era's sensitivity lives in the epoch BUDGET rather than the selection statistic.

name: aves-mlp-head
hypothesis: A shared ReLU hidden layer over FROZEN AVES recovers most of the AVES-vs-YAMNet frozen-probe gap where a linear probe cannot: AVES's per-dim buzz separation beats YAMNet's on average but PCA shows it needs ~256 directions vs YAMNet's 16 (spread thin = the case a non-linear reader should fix). Cheap decision gate for an AVES fine-tune. --hidden flag from exp/shared-trunk-head, embedder aves (cached), translation general, current val_loss stopping rule.
conclusion: IN-PIPELINE NEGATIVE, but it is a training-pathology artifact not a representation verdict. In-pipeline CV: h0 linear 0.108, h256 0.057 (0up/4down), h1024 0.091 (2up/3down), all below YAMNet cv_baseline 0.218. MLP folds early-stop at epoch 6-40 vs 18-150 linear: more params reach the val_loss argmin sooner, so the head is MORE undertrained under a rule tuned for a 768x15 linear probe on a sparse non-negative code (dropout 0.2, no weight decay) -- the aves-readout pathology amplified. Offline converged sweep (sweep_mlp.py, sklearn, standardized, to convergence): AVES linear 0.182 -> MLP(256) 0.231 (+0.049); YAMNet linear 0.248 -> MLP 0.272 (+0.024). A non-linear head helps BOTH embedders (gains on the 3 resolvable folds; 1_150/1_95 unmoved) but does NOT close the gap: AVES-MLP 0.231 < YAMNet-linear 0.248 < YAMNet-MLP 0.272, ~0.04 representation gap at every readout level. AVES fine-tune NOT motivated -- beating frozen YAMNet needs closing a gap that adding non-linearity does not touch. Incidental (matches aves-readout): converged YAMNet linear offline 0.248 vs shipped 0.218 -- the stopping rule leaves ~0.03 on the table for YAMNet too; not pursued (era keeps the current rule). trust=caveated: the logged in-pipeline number is deflated by the stopping rule; the offline number is the real signal but uses a different optimiser/convergence than the pipeline.

name: recorder-center
hypothesis: Per-deployment input centering: subtract each fold's own median embedding from its frames. Label-free and computed within one fold, so it pools nothing across folds and cannot leak. The metric already sets a threshold per site because the score scale does not transfer between deployments (1_95 at -0.401 against every other fold's -1.59 to -1.90); the claim is that non-transfer begins in the INPUT, where recorder gain, placement and ambient floor shift the whole embedding cloud. Distinct from standardize-blocks: per-DEPLOYMENT, fitted on nothing, equalising sites rather than feature blocks. Pre-registered targets 1_95 (threshold set by ~10 min of vehicle noise; a flyover is anomalous FOR THAT RECORDER) and 1_150 (buzz sits at its own ambient floor).
conclusion: NEGATIVE, and the useful part is the confound it nearly hid. Shipped 0.218 -> 0.210 (-0.008, 1 up/4 down) reads as a +0.082 hard-fold gain at 1_150 against small losses elsewhere -- exactly the shape LOOP.md says not to discount. It is an artifact: centering moved best_epoch on EVERY fold (1.4x-8.2x; 1_150 26 -> 213), and 1_150 is the fold whose early stopping was already broken, where xfold-epoch measured the epoch repair alone at +0.185. Re-scored with tools/honest_epoch.py at a cross-fold epoch, the SAME rule on both arms, no training: -0.016 (0.219 -> 0.203), 4 folds down 0 up 1 flat, and 1_150's +0.082 becomes -0.007. Negative under all four epoch rules (own-peak -0.014, shipped -0.008, xfold-median -0.017, xfold-pooled -0.016), losses led by the richest fold (53, 1031 buzz frames, -0.045 honest). BOTH pre-registered targets failed: 1_95 is -0.002 shipped / -0.014 honest. Reading: the per-site score-scale non-transfer is a readout/threshold phenomenon, not an input one -- the per-fold threshold absorbs a pure shift, and a fold's median IS close to a pure shift (only 86/1024 dims are nonzero; sparsity 0.894 -> 0.874). MECHANISM WORTH KEEPING: this is the third normalisation to blow up the epoch budget (input-standardization E2, standardize-blocks E3 at ~6x) -- treat 'any input normalisation moves the stopping epoch' as established and pair the next one with a fixed budget or cross-fold epoch rule from the start. METHOD: read best_epoch alongside every delta; when the treatment moves it, re-score both arms at a common epoch before believing the delta. --center kept, off by default, input path byte-identical when unset.

name: gain4
hypothesis: 4x waveform gain into YAMNet: a flat +log(4) lift on log-mel, hoping quiet buzz near the log_offset floor lifts more than loud negatives
conclusion: Negative (-0.028, 2up/3down). Losses concentrated on the two buzz-rich folds (1_29 -0.112, Marysville -0.063); small hard-fold gains (1_95, willard) within per-fold SD. best_epoch stable vs baseline so not a stopping artifact. Compressing top-of-range headroom hurts where buzz is dense. Do not rerun a pure gain; dynamic-range expansion is a separate untested mechanism.

name: yamnet-aves
hypothesis: YAMNet's mel frontend is not tuned to buzz and every attempt to reshape it collapses the embedding; instead concat a second, differently-encoding representation alongside it. New embedder yamnet_aves = YAMNet 1024-d (centred 0.96s) + AVES 768-d (full 1.0s) on one shared 1.0s frame grid, 1792-d, raw concat (no norm/projection so the cache is readout-agnostic). AVES alone is a clear negative (aves-probe 0.074, converged-offline 0.194 < YAMNet) but encodes buzz sparsely-concentrated vs YAMNet's 16-PC concentration -> the textbook concat case, untried because AVES was closed on its solo/replacement number. Comparator cv_baseline as aves-probe was (1.0s vs 0.96s label dilution negligible). No extraction reuse possible: yamnet (0.96s) and aves (1.0s) caches are on different frame grids.
conclusion: POSITIVE, CLEAN, REPRODUCIBLE, MODEST. Two draws (yamnet_aves CPU, yamnet_aves_2 repeat): shipped mean 0.218 -> 0.240 / 0.235; honest_epoch xfold-pooled 0.219 -> 0.243 / 0.246 (+0.024 / +0.027), stable under all four epoch rules so NOT a stopping artifact (unlike recorder-center). Same 4 folds up in both draws (1_29 +0.019/+0.053, 53 +0.027/+0.008, willard +0.050/+0.013, 1_95 +0.014/+0.024); 1_150 flat/down both (0.021->0.021/0.007) -- as context-embedder found, 1_150 needs the epoch rule not a representation. 1_95 is the FIRST intervention to move it (harmonic-comb, mech-margin, shared-trunk-head, context-embedder all flat/down there); still near-chance. Mean delta sits at probe-grid's ~0.027 single-run MDE so magnitude is at the resolution limit -- the two-draw agreement and 4-up pattern are the signal. ~half of context_embedder (+0.058 xfold-pooled) on a plain concat with the YAMNet-tuned probe. LEADS (see notes.md on exp/yamnet-aves): (1) per-block standardization -- AVES block is 3.8x the YAMNet block in per-dim |mean| (0.306 vs 0.080), 0% vs 91.6% zeros, likely underweighted under one Adam LR; --standardize exists, pair with fixed epoch budget. (2) compose with yamnet_context -- different weakness (temporal contrast vs frequency coverage), untried. Cache (560MB, 1792-d) is in the shared tree, no re-extraction needed for either.

name: yamnet-aves-head
hypothesis: Shared ReLU hidden layer (--hidden ladder h=0/256/1024) over the frozen yamnet_aves concat, in-pipeline CV; does a non-linear head beat the linear control on the 1792-d YAMNet+AVES concat.
conclusion: INCONCLUSIVE, leaning positive; confounded by the val_loss stopping rule (aves-mlp-head signature). Shipped: yav_h0 (yamnet_aves linear) 0.236, h256 0.239 (+0.003, 2up/2down/1flat), h1024 0.227 (-0.009). But best_epoch collapses monotonically with head width (1_29 100->44->29; willard 89->50->15) -> wider heads ship undertrained. honest_epoch re-score: own-peak (leaky) h0 0.247 -> h256 0.275 (+0.028) / h1024 0.264 (+0.017); xfold-median +0.006/+0.008; xfold-pooled +0.025/+0.022 -- every rule except the known-broken shipped one puts both hidden widths above linear, gain in the resolvable folds (own-peak h256 vs h0: 1_29 +0.019, willard +0.034, 1_150 +0.097 noisy). Cross-fold rules not fully trustworthy here: early-stop truncated folds at different epoch counts across arms (h0's 1_150 ended epoch 55, capping h0's pooled epoch ~55 while 1_29/53 peak 100/135), deflating h0. NOT run with a fixed epoch budget -- IDEAS' standing rule for capacity changes -- so follow-up yamnet-aves-head-fixed runs the ladder at fixed epochs. Also: yav_h0 is a 3rd draw of yamnet_aves-linear (shipped 0.236 vs logged 0.235/0.240; xfold-pooled 0.229 vs 0.243/0.246 -- low draw). yamnet_aves embedder restored + committed to main (4d9623c) this session after its embedder.py was found lost.

name: yamnet-aves-head-fixed
hypothesis: Rerun the yamnet-aves-head --hidden ladder (h=0/256/1024) on the frozen yamnet_aves concat at --fixed-epochs 150 (no early stop, no restore-best, all arms scored at one identical epoch), so the capacity question is not confounded by the val_loss stopping rule (a wider head hits its val_loss argmin sooner and ships undertrained -- the aves-mlp-head signature seen in yamnet-aves-head).
conclusion: h1024 hidden layer is +0.030 over the MATCHED FIXED-EPOCH linear control (yavf_h0 0.276 -> yavf_h1024 two-draw mean 0.307; xfold-pooled 0.275 -> 0.307), direction reproducible: r1 +0.037 (5up/0down), r2 +0.024 (4up, 1_29 flat), r1-vs-r2 -0.013 uniform across all 5 folds (seedless noise). Gain in the hard resolvable folds: two-draw mean vs h0 -- 1_150 +0.066, 53 +0.036, willard +0.032, 1_95 +0.011, 1_29 +0.006. h256 is NULL (+0.006-0.008 every rule, 3up/2down) -- width matters, a 1792->256 bottleneck buys nothing. This CONFIRMS yamnet-aves-head: the same ladder under val_loss early stopping read null-to-negative (h256 +0.003, h1024 -0.009 shipped) because best_epoch collapsed with width; the head helps the representation and early stopping hid it. INCIDENTAL AND LARGER: yavf_h0 (plain linear probe on yamnet_aves, fixed-150) is 0.276 vs the early-stopped yav_h0 0.236 -- +0.040 for the linear control from the stopping rule alone (own-peak 0.277 == shipped, so h0 plateaued by e150, not overfit). This re-measures xfold-epoch's conclusion and gives it a second motivation. Decomposition of yavf_h1024 0.307 vs cv_baseline 0.218 (+0.089), ~additive: concat +0.018, fixed-epochs +0.040, hidden-1024 +0.030. Size caveat: n=2, fixed-150 untuned, 1_150 carries ~0.066 at its ~0.055 run-to-run noise. Added --fixed-epochs flag (03_train). LEADS: compose with yamnet_context (3rd orthogonal lever); width 256<w<1024 and >1024; the fixed-epoch effect needs its own pass.
amended: 2026-09-11 (audit): headline and the h1024 verdict stand; one reading inside the conclusion does not. 'own-peak 0.277 == shipped, so h0 plateaued by e150, not overfit' is backwards -- under --fixed-epochs there is no restore-best, so own-peak == shipped means the per-fold peak sits AT the final epoch, i.e. the curve was still RISING and 150 is too short. Measured: yavf_h0's pooled sens over the last 21 epochs is +0.009 above e100-120, yavf_h1024's +0.014, and the pooled argmax lands on the 150 cap for yavf_h0. Both arms ran the same budget so the +0.030 is unaffected, but the absolute numbers are budget-limited by an unknown amount. The incidental +0.040 stopping-rule finding is confirmed and is the cleanest measurement of it in the log.

name: yamnet-aves-context
hypothesis: Compose the era's two paying representation levers: new embedder yamnet_context_aves (3840-d, [yam(t-1),yam(t),yam(t+1),aves(t)], one extraction) vs the matched yamnet_aves control, both h1024 at --fixed-epochs 150. Falsifier pre-registered: if context on top of aves gives materially less than the +0.058 context gave on plain YAMNet, the levers overlap.

baseline.model: yavf_h1024 (matched yamnet_aves h1024 fixed-150; _r2 draw 0.300, two-draw mean 0.307)

conclusion: NOT ADDITIVE, falsifier fired; and the fold pattern says do not adopt. vs the matched control's two draws (yavf_h1024 0.313 / _r2 0.300, mean 0.307): 0.321, +0.015, 2up/3down with the SAME split against each draw. Every epoch rule agrees in direction and all are inside probe-grid's ~0.027 MDE (own-peak +0.018, shipped +0.015, xfold-median +0.023, xfold-pooled +0.011). Context was +0.058 xfold-pooled on plain YAMNet, so the two levers OVERLAP -- AVES's 1.0s wav2vec2 receptive field already supplies much of what the neighbour frames do; do not budget them as independent. THE FOLD PATTERN IS THE RESULT AND IT POINTS THE WRONG WAY: the gain is entirely the two buzz-rich folds (1_29 +0.102/+0.116, ~4x its 0.024 bootstrap SD and the largest single-fold move in the era; 53 +0.011/+0.026) while ALL THREE hard folds go down against BOTH draws (willard -0.020/-0.013, 1_150 -0.035/-0.014, 1_95 -0.016/-0.009; each within its own SD but 6/6 consistent in direction). Hard folds are the target, so a lever that pays only where buzz is dense is not progress. INSTRUMENTATION, and the durable part: yamnet_context's cache carries a LABEL-CORRELATED ARTIFICIAL FEATURE -- a frame with no extracted neighbour edge-clamps, making its context block byte-identical to its centre block, at 14.0% of buzz frames vs 6.7% of negatives (measured directly in the shipped cache; base rate 12.3% buzz, 22.4% among clamped). Mechanism is structural: an isolated 1s buzz expands to a 2.592s chunk = 2 frames, both at a chunk edge, while negatives come from chunks around long annotations. 02_set/extract.py now pads every context buffer with real audio from the snip (SNIP_BUFFER_S=30) and discards the pad rows: medium cache clamp rate 0.0000 buzz / 0.0001 neg, frame roster byte-identical (79236). What the artifact was WORTH: the killed clamped run completed 2 folds on identical head/epochs/folds, and honest beats clamped (1_29 0.561->0.566, 53 0.486->0.502) -- ~0 on this metric, as predicted since fpr0.005 admits ~30 neg frames/fold and a 2-bit feature flagging 7% of negatives cannot clear that bar. So this does NOT retro-invalidate context-embedder or the context-monitor pair; but both measured folds are buzz-rich and the thin folds were never reached, so it bounds rather than closes it. SHIPPING NOTE: predict() delegates buffering to the analysis tool, so at deployment every buffer edge clamps 2 frames while training now has ~0%; the reader should overlap buffers by context_frames and discard the pad. Not checked in the buzzdetect analysis repo.
amended: 2026-09-11: BUDGET-LIMITED, and the confound runs against this entry's direction. new-era-audit (exp/pairwise-rank:notes/new-era-audit.md) found every fixed-150 run on disk still rising at its cap; pooled sens argmax is e150 for yavx_h1024 and e149 for the yavf_h1024 control. Crucially the two arms are NOT rising at the same rate: over the last 40 epochs the CONTROL gains +0.019 and this experiment's arm only +0.009, so at a longer budget the control closes on it and the +0.015 reported here could shrink to nothing or invert. The comparison as run is still matched (both arms fixed-150, one identical epoch), and the headline was already reported as inside the ~0.027 MDE with a do-not-adopt recommendation, so no conclusion changes. But the number is a 150-epoch number, not a converged one. Re-run both arms at a budget where the pooled curve has turned over before quoting this delta as the value of composing context with aves. | 2026-09-11 (2): THIRD CONTROL DRAW SETTLES THE FOLD STRUCTURE. yavf_h1024_r3 gives a 3-draw control of 0.313/0.300/0.300 (mean 0.304, headline SD 0.007; per-fold SD 0.009-0.017 -- use these, not probe-grid's 0.0095, which was measured on a different config). Against that: this entry is +0.017, and the per-fold picture resolves sharply -- 1_29 +0.105 (ELEVEN times that fold's 0.009 control SD) while all three hard folds are down by about one SD each (willard -0.011, 1_150 -0.016, 1_95 -0.008) and 53 is +0.014. So the headline is ENTIRELY 1_29. BUT 1_29 IS NOT DIAGNOSTIC OF THIS TREATMENT: pairwise-rank, which is monotonically harmful on the other four folds, puts the same fold at 0.570/0.575. Three treatment runs cluster 0.566-0.575, three control runs 0.450-0.468, no overlap. Ruled out as explanations: control noise (11x SD), undertraining (all six runs peak e72-131 on this fold and DECLINE at the cap; gap already present at e50 -- the era's 'still rising at the cap' finding is true of the pooled curve and false here), a code difference between worktrees (dataset/callbacks/sx/metrics byte-identical), and one long drone event flipping (the 259 gained frames sit in 192 separate runs, longest 5). The two treatments also gain only 47% the same frames by different distributional routes. Full write-up: diagnostics/2026-09-11_control_variance_1_29/README.md. NET READING UNCHANGED: do not adopt. The composition is not additive, and what headline it has rests on a fold whose movement is not attributable to the treatment.

name: pairwise-rank
hypothesis: mech-margin's own conclusion named its successor: that hinge was ABSOLUTE while the metric reads RANK only (every fold thresholded on its own audio), so driving mech_auto below a fixed logit buys nothing -- its share of threshold-setting FPs actually ROSE 26.5->39.3% with dose. Same target, rank-shaped: for each buzz frame sample n_pairs mech_auto frames, penalise softplus(conf - buzz + margin) on the ins_buzz logit. Dose ladder lam 0.5/2.0 on yamnet_aves + hidden 1024 + fixed-epochs 150. Target 1_95 (0.071-0.078, worst fold; 32 of 35 threshold-setting frames are mech_auto). Falsifier: if 1_95 does not move at either dose, the plainer reading of mech-margin is right and this is a loss fix to a representation problem.

baseline.model: yavf_h1024 (matched yamnet_aves h1024 fixed-150, lam=0; _r2 draw 0.300)

conclusion: CLEAR NEGATIVE, MONOTONE IN DOSE, FALSIFIER FIRED ON THE TARGET FOLD. vs matched control yavf_h1024 0.313 / _r2 0.300: lam0.5 0.280 (-0.033), lam2.0 0.246 (-0.067), 1 up / 4 down at BOTH doses, monotone in dose on 4 of 5 folds. 1_95 -- the fold this was built for -- goes 0.075 (ctrl mean) -> 0.049 -> 0.022, down and monotone, the same shape mech-margin produced at the same target. CLOSES THE buzz-vs-mech_auto LEAD IN BOTH FORMS. Every objection to mech-margin was removed here: the term is exactly scale-free (verified bit-identical under +5 on every buzz logit), same confuser class, fully in-batch over ~2 steps/epoch at size_batch 65568 so pairing is near-global, and run under --fixed-epochs so tail-loss's E2 monitor artifact (a batch-local ranking loss is invalid as val_loss) cannot fire. Result got WORSE, so the specification was not the problem. WHAT REMAINS is the plainer reading mech-margin offered and shared-trunk-head independently reached: a REPRESENTATION problem. 1_95's buzz/non-buzz mean-logit gap is 0.513 vs 1.578 at 1_29; a loss can only rotate a readout through a space that already holds the distinction. Do not spend another loss-shaped intervention on 1_95 without first showing the separation exists in the input -- the measured next step is Perch (diagnostics/2026-09-09_jet_1_95: P(jet outranks buzz) 0.860 yamnet / 0.558 aves / 0.239 perch, the only cached representation where the jet is not preferentially mistaken for buzz). COLLATERAL DAMAGE IS THE TELL: losses are not confined to the target -- 53 -0.131 and willard -0.118 at lam2.0, both monotone -- i.e. rotating away from mech_auto rotates away from buzz at sites where mech_auto was never the problem, exactly mech-margin's diagnosed mechanism. DISTRUST THE ONE FOLD THAT ROSE: 1_29 lands 0.570/0.575 (4x dose moves it 0.005) against a control at 0.464/0.450, and yamnet-aves-context -- a pure representation change with nothing in common -- put it at 0.566. Three unrelated treatments within 0.009, ~+0.11 above a control whose own draws differ by 0.014, reads as 1_29 having a second attractor the control is not in, not as three treatments helping it. yavf_h1024_r3 (third independent control draw) queued to test this; until it reports, bank no 1_29 gain in this era, including the one inside yamnet-aves-context's headline. BUDGET: all arms fixed-150 with the control's pooled curve still rising (+0.019 over last 40 epochs) vs lam0.5 nearly flat (+0.002), so a longer budget widens this negative -- the verdict is conservative as stated.
